title: Introduce staged control plane egress firewall + subnet migration operator
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add a new egress firewall operator for control plane subnets and an idempotent subnet migration operator. Backwards compatible toggle via helm values; includes Terraform module updates and an automated staged rollback path.
description: Context: Customers deploying Redwood Private at scale have run into intermittent egress path mismatches during control plane upgrades and subnet reclaim operations. This causes transient API reachability problems (control plane -> control plane egress) when route tables or NAT attachments are changed during upgrades. Motivation: provide a safe, observable, and reversible path to (1) install an egress firewall for control plane subnets, (2) migrate control plane workloads between subnets with minimal blast radius, and (3) automate rollback when reachability or health checks fail. This PR contains three coordinated deliverables: 1) an operator (installer/controllers/egress_firewall_controller.go) that reconciles host-route-based firewall rules and controls per-subnet egress ACLs with safe staging, 2) a subnet-migration operator (installer/controllers/subnet_migrator.go) that performs drain/attach/validation cycles when moving control plane instances between subnets, and 3) Terraform/Helm surface to enable the features and a staged rollout plan documented in installer/README.md. Design notes: - Staging model: feature is disabled by default. Enabling requires helm value private.egress.enabled=true and terraform var enable_egress_operator=true. - Safety: operators implement a two-phase commit for route updates (prepare -> switch -> validate -> finalize). If any validation probe fails, operator reverts to previous route and signals rollback. Validation probes include HTTPS /health checks to each control plane IP, route-table consistency checks, and synthetic traffic through the egress path. - Observability: emits metrics (controlplane.egress.switch_count, controlplane.egress.rollback_count, controlplane.subnet_migration.duration_ms) and structured audit logs with pre/post diffs for route/NACL/ENI changes. - Rollback: a /rollback job can be triggered via CR annotation or CLI; operator will run deterministic revert steps and post an incident annotation. - Upgrade choreography: includes a small upgrade hook that sequences the operator rollout with Terraform apply and Helm upgrade to avoid TOCTOU issues. Checklist: - [x] Operator core reconcile loop + unit tests - installer/controllers/*_test.go - [x] Terraform module update: terraform/modules/controlplane/egress.tf - [x] Helm chart templates + values: helm/redwood-private/templates/egress-firewall.yaml and values.yaml default=false - [x] Integration test harness exercises staged switch and rollback in perf-canary cluster - [x] Docs: installer/README.md with rollout/rollback steps and risk matrix - [x] Observability: metrics + opentracing spans - [x] Security review: minimal IAM surface for operator (assume role to modify route tables, ENIs) Known limitations / future work: - Does not yet support cross-account route table ownership (follow-up ENG-4012). - BGP-based on-prem egress is out of scope for this PR. Related: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3921/control-plane-egress-operator, terraform module family update ENG-3958.
